raw_response:
I am sixty years old this year, and I have never been to school. I cannot read those papers the extension people hand out, but I know my land. I farm about seven mu here in Quzhou, and I do what my neighbors do — that is how I have survived all these years.

This year, I will grow winter wheat and summer maize on the same plots, like always. The wheat went in last October after I ran the rotary tiller through the fields. I bought improved wheat seed from the shop in town — I do not save my own seed anymore because the shop seed grows better. For fertilizer, I put down two bags of compound fertilizer per mu and one bag of ammonium bicarbonate as the base dressing. My neighbor across the road uses about the same, and his wheat is always thick and green. If I use less, I worry — a bad year would hurt more than wasting a few yuan on extra fertilizer. I will irrigate three times: the winter water, the green-up water, and the jointing water. If I see aphids or weeds, I spray. Last year I sprayed five times for wheat and that kept the bugs away.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, there is barely a week before I must plant the maize. There is no time to plough — we plant straight into the wheat stubble, no-tillage. I will buy hybrid maize seed, Nongda or Denghai, whatever they have at the shop. For the maize, I will put down about one and a half bags of the 28-6-6 compound fertilizer per mu. That gives the maize a good start. I will irrigate twice if the summer is dry, and spray three or four times when the bugs come. I used to grow cotton, but I am too old for all that bending and picking now. Wheat and maize are my insurance — even if one fails, the other usually feeds us. I expect about 1000 kilos per mu for wheat and about 950 for maize if the weather holds.
